stances_toward.note: Rival, not adversary, by the ontology rule that the grade follows the sources. The brief suggested adversary; no source read says the Mexican state seeks the cartels' defeat or disappearance, and Sheinbaum explicitly denies that the cartels pursue political objectives (Aug 2025), which is the reason she rejects the terrorist label (the FTO designations of Feb 2025 and the additions of July 2026). Competing interests, violence against the state, no will to destroy the other side as a political actor. Trend cooling as the designations grow and the US pressure to act against cartels in Mexico hardens. Since 1 Oct 2024 (Sheinbaum's term); the confrontation predates her. Sharpened 2026-10-16 (the state does fight the cartels when it chooses to). Mexican special forces killed CJNG leader El Mencho on 22 Feb 2026 in Tapalpa, Jalisco, with US intelligence support (White House, Mexican defence ministry; Sheinbaum says no US troops took part), and the retaliation burned vehicles and blocked roads in several states. That is rival on a war footing, not adversary, since no source reads the aim as the cartels' disappearance as an order, and the state also transfers prisoners rather than only killing leaders. Trend stays cooling.

relations_to.summary: On 22 Feb 2026 Mexican special forces, with support from the air force and National Guard, killed CJNG leader Nemesio 'El Mencho' Oseguera in Tapalpa, Jalisco; the White House confirmed intelligence support, the defence secretary said Mexico benefited from US agencies, and Sheinbaum said no US troops took part. CJNG retaliated with burned vehicles and road blocks in Jalisco and other states and the US and Canadian embassies issued shelter-in-place warnings. Sheinbaum told Trump the next day that coordination was going 'very well'. An OSAC assessment of 9 Oct 2026 looks at whether the cartel changed.
